monitoring.description: Enable device-mapper event monitoring for activation (e.g., thin pool status, LV lock status). Disable only in minimal environments or debugging.

min_initial_size.description: Minimum free space (in MiB) required in a volume group before activating logical volumes. Helps prevent out-of-space failures.

activation_retry.description: Maximum seconds to wait for an LV to become free before failing activation. Increase for systems with slow I/O or high contention.

use_polling.description: Use polling instead of asynchronous device-mapper event notifications for activation checks. Avoid unless dm-notify is unavailable.

read_only.description: Activate all logical volumes in read-only mode by default. Useful for disaster recovery or testing scenarios.

auto_activation_volume_list.description: List of volume or LV names (patterns or exact) that should be auto-activated on boot. Empty list = all eligible LVs auto-activate.

raid.min_home_pages.description: Minimum number of RAID home pages (metadata pages) required before RAID LV activation. Prevents degraded RAID activation if metadata is too sparse.

raid.sync_max.description: Maximum number of sync operations LVM will attempt before aborting RAID rebuild/resync.

mirror.log_failures.description: Log failures of mirror logs (e.g., when metadata is lost). Helps diagnose mirror inconsistencies.

mirror.auto_recovery.description: Automatically recover failed mirror images (if possible) after activation. Disable if manual intervention preferred.

mirror.min_recovery_rate.description: Minimum number of mirror images required to be healthy before mirror LV activates. Prevents activation of critically degraded mirrors.

thin_pool.metadata_read_ahead.description: Read-ahead (in sectors) for thin pool metadata devices. 0 = use kernel default.

thin_pool.check_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for thin pool health check before treating pool as unhealthy (e.g., near full).

thin_pool.error_when_full.description: Fail activation of thin pool when pool is full (or near full). Set false to allow activation in degraded mode.

scan.description: List of device filters (regexes with a=accept, r=reject) to determine which block devices LVM scans for PVs.

preferred_names.description: List of device name patterns (regexes) used to prefer one path over others in multipath setups.

filtering.description: Enable device filtering via the scan rules above. Disable only for debugging or trusted environments.

md_component_detection.description: Detect and exclude Linux MD RAID components to avoid confusion between LVM PVs and MD arrays.

aliases.description: Optional device alias mappings (e.g., multipath wwid → /dev/mapper/...) for consistent naming.

backup.backup.description: Enable automatic backup of LVM metadata before modifications (e.g., lvcreate, vgreduce).

backup.backup_dir.description: Directory to store per-VG metadata backups. Should be on a reliable filesystem.

backup.archives.description: Number of old metadata archives to retain per volume group. Older archives are pruned automatically.

backup.archive_prefix.description: Prefix for archive filenames (usually 'vgname' or 'lvmbackup'). Archives named: vgname_timestamp

activation_hooks.description: List of activation event hooks (e.g., 'pre_pvmove', 'post_lvcreate'). Each hook executes a shell command.

description.description: Human-readable purpose of the hook (used only for inline comments).

event.description: LVM activation event to hook into (e.g., 'pre_lvcreate', 'post_vgchange').

command.description: Shell command to run on event. Can use environment variables (e.g., $VG_NAME, $LV_NAME).

log.verbose.description: Log verbosity: 0=errors only, 1=warnings, 2=info, 3=debug. Higher values produce more detail.

log.prefix.description: String prefix for all LVM log messages (e.g., '[LVM2] ').

log.syslog.description: Send LVM logs to system syslog (true) or to a file (false).

log.file.description: Path to file for logs when syslog=false. Requires write permission.

log.overwrite.description: Overwrite log file (true) or append (false) when logging to a file.

log.level.description: Global minimum log level (0=error, 1=warn, 2=info, 3=debug). Only messages ≥ this level are logged.
